clue.text: Poor Arab gets stoned when protecting daughter — a crowd gathers

indicators.note: a crowd that gathers something holds it, so these letters go around what follows

parts.note: from the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd', a crowd is three

indicators.note: what protects stands around something, so the shuffled letters wrap the next piece
someone stoned is intoxicated and all over the place, so the word Arab is rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor Arab is stoned by a gathering mob for shielding his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets stoned' makes ABAR, which holds D; 'Poor' looks like pity for the Arab but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: clothing worn thin from long use looks poor and shabby.

clue.text: In jam, strike rear of car, resulting in whiplash

indicators.note: to strike something out is to delete it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a jam of people is a throng

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A rear-end shunt in a traffic jam leaves a driver with whiplash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear of car' is R, struck from THRONG.
explanation.definitionFit: The lash of a whip is its thong, the leather strip that cracks.

clue.text: Votes on free movement — new bill is written up

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: movement of letters means they are rearranged
in a down clue, written upwards means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an ad is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: Votes on free movement of people with a new bill being drafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' shuffles FREE into FERE; 'written up' turns AD into DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Latin-derived word for a public ballot on a single question, which are votes.

clue.text: In rain dance, am I performing?

definitions.text: In rain dance, am I performing?

indicators.note: letters performing put on a new show, rearranging themselves

explanation.surface: A dancer wonders whether a rain dance counts as a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of the answer: a rain dance is a ritual associated with Native American peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain dances are ceremonies traditionally performed by some Native American peoples, so the performer is described.

clue.text: Lionel receives acting tip for minor role

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Lionel Bart was the English composer who wrote the musical Oliver!

indicators.note: letters acting up behave wildly, so tip is rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer gets some acting advice about playing a small part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acting' shuffles TIP into ITP, which BART receives.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a small part in a play or film, with few lines.

clue.text: One could provide venison, caviar and honey, say …

parts.note: caviar is fish roe

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: honey and dear are both terms of endearment

explanation.surface: A menu listing venison, caviar and honey as luxury ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: venison is deer meat, and this small European deer is hunted for it.

clue.text: Lacking source of cash, chooses to make a comeback — boxers tend to do this

indicators.note: coming back means going the other way, so the letters are read backwards
lacking something means having it taken away

parts.note: picks means chooses

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A boxer short of money decides on a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: PICKS lacking C is PIKS, which turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers famously train by jumping rope, an activity also called skipping.

clue.text: … so with a couple of thousand I launched small retail outlet

indicators.note: here one piece comes with the other wrapped around it

parts.note: K is a thousand, so two thousand is two Ks

indicators.note: launched letters are sent flying and land rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, someone starts a small shop with two thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launched' shuffles SO and I into IOS, which sits between the two Ks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small booth or stall selling newspapers, sweets or tickets.

clue.text: Cruise company recruits female crew at a number of remarkable events

indicators.note: recruiting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: P&O is a British cruise and ferry company
a hen is a female bird
a crew is the men of a ship

explanation.surface: A cruise line hires women for its crew at several notable events.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a word for an extraordinary occurrence or marvel.

clue.text: In which you may find chocolate drops?

definitions.text: In which you may find chocolate drops?

parts.words: In which you may find chocolate drops?
parts.note: chocolate drops suggest little sweets, but here a chocolate bar drops out of a coin-operated dispenser

explanation.surface: A question about where small chocolate sweets might be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated dispenser lets a chocolate bar fall down when you pay.

clue.text: Rum and sour cream

parts.note: milk gone sour has gone off
to cream an opponent is to beat them soundly

explanation.surface: A cocktail of rum with soured cream.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum here is the British adjective for odd or strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rum, in British slang, means peculiar or unconventional.

clue.text: Extremists in Europe surely facing zero resistance when entering? It doesn't look good

indicators.note: pieces entering go inside the outer letters
the extremists of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: yes, surely! is an assent
O looks like zero
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Politicians at Europe's fringes face no opposition entering, which looks bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something ugly that offends the sight, such as a building that spoils a view.

clue.text: Shoot airmen and get out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to fire at the pilots and flee.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: a seed sprouts or puts out a shoot when it begins to grow.

clue.text: Look, with the introduction of ceiling, you'll have two floors

indicators.note: the clue runs in reverse: the answer with a letter added gives the two floors, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: to deck someone is to floor them, and a KO (knockout) floors them too

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Adding a ceiling to a building gives you a two-storey house.
explanation.walkthrough: Put C into the answer and you get DECK and KO, two ways to floor someone; so take C out of those.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a quick glance, as in 'have a dekko'.

clue.text: Girl's brought over something to get you going!

indicators.note: brought over means flipped, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Anne's is a girl's name with the possessive

explanation.surface: A girl's home-brought pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant extract used as a laxative, so it gets your bowels moving; a playful description.

clue.text: When it was assumed remorse was being shown, idiot blocked fire hydrant

definitions.text: When it was assumed remorse was being shown

indicators.note: something blocked has a piece stuck inside it

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
H marks a fire hydrant on British street signs
a clot is an idiot

explanation.surface: An idiot blocks a fire hydrant, and supposedly regrets it.
explanation.walkthrough: Assumed means put on: penitents traditionally wore this cloth with ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitents put on coarse goat-hair cloth, with ashes, as a sign of repentance.

clue.text: Intern, say, has to work for bully

indicators.note: letters put to work are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An intern is made to work for a bullying boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to rule or treat others cruelly and oppressively.

clue.text: Clint Eastwood's opening shot captures soldiers showing no mercy

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside
shot means broken, so the letters are rearranged
a word's opening is its first letter

parts.note: men are soldiers

explanation.surface: A Clint Eastwood western opens with a merciless shootout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' makes INCLET from the actor's first name plus the opening letter of Eastwood.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal sense: harsh, merciless; the word is now mostly used of stormy weather.

clue.text: Conservative and Liberal's identifying title in office, leaders together accepted

definitions.text: Conservative and Liberal's identifying title in office, leaders together accepted

indicators.note: the letters are put together into a new order
the leaders of words are their first letters

parts.words: Conservative and Liberal's identifying title in office

parts.note: on means accepted, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: The Tory-Lib Dem government's name while they held power jointly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2010-15 UK government of Conservatives and Liberal Democrats was known by the answer. 'together' shuffles CALITIO into COALITI.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2010 British government was a two-party alliance that went by this name.

clue.text: In hospital, facing real trouble, one's required to assist with breathing

definitions.text: one's required to assist with breathing

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital patient in real trouble needs help to breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: An asthma puffer is a device used to draw medicine into the lungs.

clue.text: Fox News screening nothing positive

indicators.note: screening something hides it behind, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: N is new, so news is two of them
O looks like nothing, zero
plus means positive

explanation.surface: The American TV channel airs nothing upbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Fox is a verb here, to baffle, not the network.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to fox someone is to bewilder or perplex them.

clue.text: Bloke's taken short after second coffee

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: taken short means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a chap is a bloke

explanation.surface: A man caught short after his second cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken short' is British for urgently needing a toilet; here it trims CHAP to CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a chocolate-flavoured coffee, named after a Yemeni port.

clue.text: Make milky coffee, initially tasteless

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter

parts.note: loud clothes are garish, tasteless

explanation.surface: Instructions to add milk to coffee that has no flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to make a liquid cloudy, opaque or milky in appearance.

clue.text: Lacking in name, inventor somehow gets patent

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are rearranged in some way
lacking means without, so letters are taken away

explanation.surface: An inventor without a name still obtains a patent.
explanation.walkthrough: INVENTOR minus I, N and N leaves VETOR, which 'somehow' shuffles. Patent is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: patent means plainly evident, open to view.

clue.text: Hot and cold stuff containing key skin treatment

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: containing means holding inside

parts.note: to stuff is to ram, cram
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A lotion of hot and cold ingredients with a key ingredient for skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a moisturising lotion applied to the hands to soften dry skin.

clue.text: One's reluctant to spend money in motorway services, having mostly been ripped off

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, read as MI

indicators.note: most of the word services is torn away, keeping only its start

explanation.surface: A tightwad complains about prices at a motorway service station.
explanation.walkthrough: Motorway services are British roadside rest stops, notorious for overpricing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hoarder who hates parting with cash.

clue.text: Generally speaking, one has nothing against the Queen at all

parts.note: O looks like nothing, zero
V is short for versus, against
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarchist protests they have nothing at all against the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverbial synonym: taken as a whole, on the whole, in general.

clue.text: In the US, measures taken to restrain old lags

indicators.note: restraining means holding inside

parts.note: liters is the American spelling of litres, measures of volume

explanation.surface: American measures to restrain old convicts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lags' is British slang for veteran prisoners; here lags is the verb, dawdles.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to lag is to fall behind or dawdle idly.

clue.text: African dwelling on edge of plateau

parts.note: a hut is a simple dwelling

indicators.note: edge picks the end letter

explanation.surface: An African home perched on the edge of a high plateau.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of a people of Rwanda and Burundi.

clue.text: Hoping to exploit resources, one searches for busy ports outside of European Community

definitions.text: Hoping to exploit resources, one searches

parts.note: pro means for, in favour

indicators.note: being outside means surrounding the other piece
busy letters are bustling about, rearranged

parts.note: EC is the European Community

explanation.surface: A mining explorer searching busy harbours outside the EC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' makes SPTOR, which goes outside the Community's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone searching for gold or minerals to mine.
